settings.name_in_paper: Action-centered contextual bandit with probability constraints
unmapped: Reward = arbitrary time-varying, nonlinear baseline g_t(context) (no assumptions, may change abruptly) plus a fixed linear treatment effect s_{t,a}^T theta for nonzero actions; the baseline action 0 has zero treatment effect
Learner's policy must play a nonzero action with probability in [pi_min, pi_max] (0<pi_min<=pi_max<1), and regret is measured against the optimal probability-constrained policy
Contexts chosen by an adversary based on the history
settings.definition_quote: E[r_t(\bar{s}_t,a_t) | \bar{s}_t,a_t] =\bar{f}_t(\bar{s}_t,a_t) = f(s_{t,a_t}) I(a_t > 0) + g_t(\bar{s}_t) ... r_t(a_t) - r_t(0) = s_{t,a_t}^T \theta I(a_t > 0) + n_t where n_t is zero-mean sub-Gaussian noise with variance \sigma^2 ... We constrain 0< \pi_{\min} \leq 1-\mathbb{P}(a_t = 0|\bar{s}_t) \leq \pi_{\max} < 1

bound.regime: for any 0 < eps_alg < 1, 0 < delta < 1; holds with probability at least 1 - 3*delta/2

symbols.C_thm: constant given in the proof (depends on noise level R and on C_pi = sqrt(min(pi_min(1-pi_max), pi_max(1-pi_min))))

conditions: baseline and interaction rewards bounded (by one)
nonzero-action probability constrained to [pi_min, pi_max] with pi_min, pi_max bounded away from 0 and 1
baseline g_t arbitrary and time-varying; contexts chosen adversarially given history

source.quote: Consider the action-centered contextual bandit problem, where $g_t$ is potentially time varying, and $\bar{s}_t$ at time $t$ given $\mathcal{H}_{t-1}$ is chosen by an adversary. Under this regime, the total regret at time $T$ for the action-centered Thompson sampling contextual bandit (Algorithm 1) satisfies \[ \mathcal{R}(T) \leq C \left(\frac{d^2}{\epsilon} \sqrt{T^{1+\epsilon}}(\log(Td) \log \frac{1}{\delta})\right) \] with probability at least $1-3\delta/2$, for any $0< \epsilon < 1$, $0< \delta < 1$. The constant $C$ is in the proof.

results.notes: Regret is sum_t (pi*_t s_{t,a*}^T theta - pi_t s_{t,abar_t}^T theta), against the optimal probability-constrained policy; bound holds w.p. >= 1-3delta/2. Paper remarks that epsilon = 1/log T gives O(d^2 sqrt(T)) and the bound is independent of N. Theorem epsilon is an analysis/tuning parameter (enters v), mapped to eps_alg. Environment mapped to adversarial_restricted due to arbitrary time-varying baseline; horizon recorded as anytime since the algorithm does not take T as input (but eps=1/log T tuning would require T).
